Website Timeline Update and The “Shared Epilogue”

So, when the timeline updated on the Japanese Zelda site, many (including the YouTuber Zeltik) were excited to see that within the website's source code, the Wild era games (BotW and TotK) were categorized as a "shared epilogue" at the end of all three timelines.

Many fans have taken this as a potential confirmation of the "convergence" theory—the idea that somehow, somewhere down the line, all three timelines merged into one before the events of Breath of the Wild. 

However, looking at it from a web development and structural perspective, calling it a "shared epilogue" is literally just a functional CSS/code tag used to display the Wild era games universally at the bottom of the page regardless of which timeline path you scroll down.

What would this mean for Hyrule? The first convergence would be about reconciling different histories. The second would be about reconciling, or confronting, different realities. That raises an interesting question: can these worlds coexist without one having to erase or overwrite the others?

Why the Green River Zoras appeared only in the downfall timeline theory.

In Oracle of Ages the green Zoras were referred to as the river Zoras, basically a different sub species of zora that inhabit fresh water lakes and rivers.

I came up with this theory on why the Green River Zoras only appeared in the downfall timeline, and why the Zoras in Ocarina of Time looked so different now.

When Ganondorf ruled Hyrule he changed the waters in Hyrule to be less salty, akin to removing the extra chlorine in the water, or removing its density at least compared to the regular water we see in Ocarina of Time when Link was a child. But it also lead to the Zora to slowly evolve to accommodate this water. The first few generations looked the same, so they took no interest in the water. But their biology was slowly changing in each generation to better reflect it, such as having more fishy features and such.

The reason why don't see the river Zora in the adult timeline is because of the great flood so the Zora couldn't change into the river Zora, but instead they changed into the Rito.

The reason why we don't see the river Zoras in the child timeline is because Link was sent back to his childhood, so Ganondorf couldn't tamper with the water so the Zora remained the same.

[ALL] What are some theories/headcanons about the lore that you have or believe?

For the past few days I've been posted some strange theories about Zelda lore.

Most of them are pretty much "X became X" or "X is the same as X", which some of you don't like. So, now I'm gong to take a break and ask if there are any theories or headcanon about the lore you want to share?

I'll start.

Leviathans reproduce by dreaming, much like Beholders from D&D. The Wind Fish has the power to created realistic worlds by dreaming. On rare occasions, these dreams become so vivid, it produces a new real leviathan.

P.S. The Leviathan thing was going to be a whole post. But I realised there's not enough evidence to make it more then a headcanon. So, I just made it a post saying "This is my bizarre headcanon. You can ignore it if you want. But you can tell me yours" post.

I think some of us needed to go from imaginative teenagers to adults before we thought harder about this, but I'll just make it clear:

Isn't it obvious to most people by now, that every time a new Zelda game came out it shifted what you thought was the current timeline? Given that you have to reinvent and rethink the entire timeline every time a new game is made, that puts into question what we already locked in stone as the previous operating-theory, what's the point of repeating that process?

You know that whatever Timeline you come up with only lasts until Breath of the Wild 3, when nothing fits together, again. For the third time.

At some point you realize that all the timeline ever was, was mental gymnastics, and in the end you may also start to suspect there isn't really any point to the timeline.

What is the point of the timeline, and what's even the reason to make one if the games never actually connect with any purpose?

[All] Religions of Hyrule Part 1: Humans

This is a post about the religions of Hyrule. This is going to be multiple parts. I don't know how many yet.

The Three Goddesses
Bit of an introduction.
The three most important deities of Hyrule are the Three Golden Goddess. Din, Nayru and Farore.
These three are the creators of the Zelda universe. And, along with the Triforce, appear to be worshiped by every race in some shape or form. Although, different races may place different levels of enthesis on a certain Goddess.

Hylia, Hylians and the Shiekah
Other then the Golden Goddesses, the main deity of the Hylians is the unseen goddess, Hylia, in which the Hylians get their name.
In addition to the statues and springs, Hylia is also worshiped through her decendents, the Hyrulian Royal Family. The most famous members being the various Princesses Zelda, all named after the mortal reincarnation of Hylia. (I'm NOT saying "All Zeldas are Hylia". I'm only saying they are named after her). This was already a tradition as confirmed by King Rhoam. Although a Prince in AoL briefly made it "law". The Princessess Zelda also seem to be priestesses.
The Shiekah are a subset of Hylians, who guard the Royal Family. This tradition presumably coming from SS Impa being Hylia's servant.

Trees and Leviathans
Although the Deku Tree is known for being the guardian of the Kokiri/Koroks (who I'll get to in another part), he is an important figure in Hylian culture, something made more clear in later games. In BotW he guards the Master Sword, and in EoW he guards the Triforce.
I previously made a post on how the Forest Temple of OoT may have been built by humans to worship the spirits of the forest. Specifically, the Deku Tree.
The Maku Trees I may discuss in the future.
We also have Levias, the Guardian of Skyloft. A figure revered by the Hylians (at the time, simply called "humans") who would be offered against bowl of Pumpkin Soup.
Leviathans would loose relevance amongst Hylians in the future. Ignoring the Wind Fish, who's significance to Hyrule, if any, is unknown and the Ocean King, who is the god of is own world, most Leviathan worship would be practiced by the Zora.
A possible exception by be Jabun in the WW. Whilst not confirmed, is assumed to have been worshiped by Hylians on Greatfish Isle. This would make sense, due to the flood making sea travel more important.

Gerudo
Unlike other humans in Hyrule, the Gerudo don't worship Hylia (maybe except briefly in the past) or the Royal Family. Instead, the main focus of their religion is "Ancestor worship".
The Goddess of Sand is often assumed to be an aspect of Din, but other theories suggest it may be a personification of the Gerudo ancestor. It's possible this figure might represent the founding member of Hyrule's Gerudo settlement.
The Hylians once believed the Goddess of the Sand to be "evil", but only because they were still enemies with the Gerudo at the time.

Part 2 is here: [All] Religions of Hyrule Part 2: Zora and Rito

[OoT] Lore behind the Skull Mask

The Skull Mask us one of eight masks you can wear in OoT. At first glance, it doesn't seem like much. Just a funny mask, nothing more.

However, if you talk to certain people, specifically, those in the woods, you can find some potential lore for the mask.

When talking to Saria, she'll say the mask reminds us of something she saw in the woods. At first, I thought she was talking about Skull Kid. But this is before we sell the mask to him. You Could say this is an oversight, but I think it's more likely meant to be a hint of who to sell the mask to.

Fado will compare you to a "Forest Ghost".

The most intresting one is the Deku scrubs in the Forest Stage. they reward you with more Deku Sticks, as the mask resembles their "sacred forest totem".

Theory

So, who or what is the skull mask based on? For Fado, it could just be a reference to the Stalfos, which she confirms to know about.

I noticed that the mask looks like a simplified version of the mask Phantom Ganon wore. Phantom Ganon being the boss of the Forest Temple.

Of course, it's unlikely Phantom Ganon is the figure Saria and the Deku Scrubs are talking about. However, it's possible that Ganondorf may have used a similar mask when requiting the Deku Scrubs to invade the Deku Tree.

The Deku appear to be your typical "false idol worshipers". This is shown in OoT when they regard Ghoma as their "queen", and later shown in FSA, when they worship Ganon, who, coincidentally, also places a Phantom of himself in the local Temple.

It's possible Ganondorf appeared to the Deku wearing the mask, claiming to be their god and appointing Ghoma as their queen. Saria, who spends a lot of time in the Lost Woods, may have seem a glimpse if this, but may not have thought of it. She may have just thought he was a regular forest spirit.

In the adult half, Ganondorf would create Phantom Ganon, based on himself as the "Forest Totem".

EDIT:

somebody suggested they might actually see the Stalfos as their "Forest Totem". Ganondorf may have still used a mask to trick the Deku into thinking he was their god.

Are all Gerudo descendants of Groose and Impa? Skyward Sword theory

The Gerudo are notably absent from the events of Skyward Sword. I've always wondered why that is the case, since Nintendo ensured that there was an origin for the Gorons, the Zora, the Kokiri, and even Mogmas. When I first reached Lanayru, I was expecting to see the precursor to the Gerudo tribe- instead, we are met with the first automated and non-biological species: the LD Robot series. It is clear that these robots are not the ancestors of the Gerudo, for multiple reasons. They are non-living and their purpose of harvesting timeshift stones is exclusive to them, not passed down through time. In fact, the common trait of dark skin that is associated with the Gerudo tribe is all but absent from one character: Impa. However, she does not feature two other prominent Gerudo traits: red hair and amber eyes. Do you know who does possess such features? Groose. I don't love the idea that Groose started a family with granny Impa but I also don't think it was possible for him to start a family with young Impa. All this is to ask you folks a question: what do you believe happened? Is there an alternate origin for the Gerudo or is it strictly implied through Impa and Groose?

The worst part of losing the old 3D Zelda style of games, is that there is nothing out there to replace it.

By throwing most known Zelda elements out of the window with the Wild era games, the franchise has lost an identity and style of game that was unique to it. That dungeon crawling style of gameplay with long tighly designed puzzle boxes dungeons and their overwhelming atmosphere + item progression; is something that hasnt been able to be replicated in any other game, especially in 3D

2D Zelda clones there has been many of them, some of them are quite good, and others not so much. But the 3D ones, there is simply nothing like it. Some could say Okami or Darksiders, but... is not really the same, and these are already pretty old games. There has been some indies with some projects pending, but get lost in the process.

And is frustrating when you see fans of other franchises like Final Fantasy, who also changed and had their own fanbases divided aswell, but guess what? Atleast they got games like the current aclaimed Expedition 33 that pandered to older FF fans, or Baldurs Gate, or the Bravely Default series. But us older Zelda fans, especially from the OOT to SS era, got nothing like that.

Where could the cave leading to Ganondorf be located?

Recently, I actually went wandering through Hyrule Castle. I tried to find any possible clues that could help point to where Ganondorf might be held. I thought of 3 places.

The main hall: This area is mysteriously blocked off in BOTW, even though it's a massive part of the castle. There's an obvious doorway leading to it, but boulders block it. Perhaps they open it in the sequel and discover a way down to his chamber.

The circular room where you fight Calamity Ganon: This one makes a bit more sense, since it's the furthest area beneath the castle. Though it doesn't seem like there would be any openings to reach him from there.

One of the passages at the bottom of the castle: This would be places like the prison, or where you unlock the hidden shrine. There could easily be some kind of hidden opening somewhere. There's a lot of stone walls, and rocks that could easily be moved to reveal a passageway. Where specifically though, I have no idea.

It's just something I've been thinking about a lot. His body was right under us the whole time and we had no clue.. until the BOTW2 trailer.

Majora's mask helped me understand why I dislike BotW/TotK

To be brief, I'll just say that Majora's Mask and other games from that era incentivize you to explore not just for exploration sake but to progress in the game. And that's because Majora's Mask is much more cryptic and subtle in the hints it gives you. It won't just tell you "go there", will not repeat helpful information, Tatl will not even help you like Navi and there's no dot on the map or quest log to remind you what to do. These can all be viewed as negatives, but to me, that's when I enjoy exploring, because I actually need to do it to beat the game, not just waste time in a video game.

BotW just tells you "there's all of this you can do, here's exactly where you have to go to do it, but really if you want to beat the game just go there, you won't be scratching your head over how to get there, it's just that you have 1 chance in a million because it's difficult." I don't care about exploration in this context, if I don't have to do something to beat a game I'm unlikely to do it. Sure that's content I paid for that I'm missing, but I'm also not watching every movie on Netflix just because I paid for a subscription.

I understand why a lot of people don't view Majora's Mask in a good light, it's not for everyone, and I think the cryptic nature is actually a turnoff for a lot of people. But I think these cryptic hints were the reason I explored the small world of Termina much more than other games that just clearly spell out what you have to do. I think Skyward Sword needed to be just as cryptic as Majora's Mask, because of how small the world is, instead of Fi constantly telling you where to go.

[All] What are some examples of gods, demigods and deitys in this franchise?

The Zelda franchise is a fantasy franchise with a lot of magical creatures/characters. However, in a series with a bunch of characters with impressive powers, which characters are actualy considered gods/demigods/deitys?

Like obviously we have the 3 Golden Godesses and Hylia as gods, however is Demise considered a god, or is he more of a demigod? Then what about the Sand godess in the Spirit Temple? Is that a real godess or just something the Gerudo worship?

Again, what about demigods? Which characters would be considered demigods? Demise, as i mentioned, and the Fierce Deity. What about the dragons in Skyward Sword? Would they be considered demigods, or simply deities, along with the dragons in the Wild Era? Or the Fairy Queen in Wind Waker? What about the Light Spirits in Twilight Princess?

As for deitys? We have Satori from BotW/TotK which is confirmed to be a deity. But are there others that would be considered deities? Great Fairies, The Ocean King, Deku Tree, Valoo, Lord JabuJabu and Jabuun definetly have the status as deities. But what about characters such as Zelda, Fi, Levias, The Wind Fish, Majora, Link or the like. Would they be considered deities, or simply just really powerful beings?
